chunks: And from him, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Mihran al-Jammal, who said:
I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when he prayed and finished his prayer, he raised both his hands entirely above his head.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) raise his hands after finishing the prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi highlights the practice of raising both hands above the head upon concluding the prayer, a detail often discussed in the context of *raf' al-yadayn* and its variations among Shia jurists. It underscores the meticulous attention to physical etiquette (*adab*) in the Imam’s worship, serving as a primary evidence for the recommended nature of this gesture at the end of the *salat*. The report reflects the broader Shia emphasis on emulating the Prophet and Imams in every aspect of ritual precision.
